end.summary:
- Practised naming polygons by counting sides: triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon and octagon; some names still need checking for steadiness.
- Recognised triangles and polygons in different positions and sizes, including rotated and folded examples; this was shown on a new-situation question.
- Practised describing triangles using equal sides and right angles; why-based or new-situation examples still need checking.
- Used the ideas of straight sides, a closed shape, side count and 90° angles.
end.parentNote: Veer practised naming polygons by counting sides and used straight sides, closed shapes and side count to recognise shapes even when they were turned or different sizes. They also described equilateral and right-angled triangles using equal sides and a 90° angle; these descriptions still need a why-based or new-situation check. There was no recorded mix-up that needed later correction. At home, show a few turned or unusual shapes and ask Veer to name them and explain which features helped.
